name: Levelland Texas
summary: Quince automovilistas independientes alrededor de Levelland (Texas) reportaron en tres horas un objeto oval que apagaba motores y faros al acercarse, con los sistemas restaurándose al alejarse; el sheriff Weir Clem lo confirmó en la escena. Primer evento masivo de interferencia electromagnética documentado.
summary_en: Within three hours, fifteen independent drivers around Levelland, Texas reported an oval object that killed engines and headlights on approach, with systems recovering as it left; sheriff Weir Clem confirmed it at the scene. The first documented mass electromagnetic-interference event.

evidenceContribution.rationale: Múltiples vehículos independientes en Levelland TX experimentaron stalls + EM interference + observación de objeto luminoso. Sheriff Weir Clem y deputies independientemente confirmaron observaciones en diferentes locations dentro del área en mismo período (90 minutos). El pattern multi-vehicular EM no es producible por ball lightning o plasma localizado (que no causaría stalls sostenidos en múltiples vehículos a millas de distancia). Modest porque sin radar ni telemetría — evidencia es testimonial multi-witness + sheriff.
evidenceContribution.rationaleEn: Multiple independent vehicles in Levelland TX experienced stalls + EM interference + observation of a luminous object. Sheriff Weir Clem and deputies independently confirmed observations at different locations within the area during the same window (90 minutes). The multi-vehicle EM pattern is not producible by ball lightning or localized plasma (which wouldn't cause sustained stalls in multiple vehicles miles apart). Modest because no radar or telemetry — evidence is multi-witness testimonial + sheriff.

evidenceContribution.rationale: Pattern 8k (interferencia EM) documentado en su forma más clara: múltiples vehículos stalled simultáneamente en proximidad de objeto luminoso. La interferencia electromagnética sostenida a través de varios vehículos independientes en kilómetros sugiere física no convencional. Marco Puthoff/Davis: interferencia EM como firma de propulsión exótica. Modest porque sin medición física directa del campo EM.
evidenceContribution.rationaleEn: Pattern 8k (EM interference) documented in its clearest form: multiple vehicles stalled simultaneously near a luminous object. Sustained electromagnetic interference across several independent vehicles over kilometers suggests non-conventional physics. Puthoff/Davis framework: EM interference as signature of exotic propulsion. Modest because no direct physical EM field measurement.

whatHappened:
Entre las 22:50 del 2 de noviembre y las 01:30 del 3 de noviembre de 1957, el sheriff Weir Clem del condado de Hockley en Texas recibió 15 llamadas independientes de automovilistas en un radio de 16 km alrededor de Levelland. Todos reportaban el mismo fenómeno: un objeto oval brillante en o cerca de la carretera, sus motores se detuvieron y los faros se apagaron al aproximarse; al alejarse el objeto los sistemas se restauraban espontáneamente.

El sheriff Clem y su ayudante condujeron a la escena y observaron ellos mismos un objeto rojo-naranja brillante antes de que se elevara y desapareciera. Pedro Saucedo, primer testigo del evento, había detenido su vehículo por miedo al impacto; su motor y luces fallaron mientras el objeto pasaba sobre el vehículo, y se restauraron tras la salida.

Project Blue Book investigó y atribuyó el evento a 'ball lightning' — explicación insuficiente para 15 automovilistas independientes con efectos eléctricos repetibles sobre vehículos diferentes durante tres horas en clima atmosféricamente normal (sin tormenta eléctrica reportada). La investigación del Dr. James McDonald (Universidad de Arizona) en 1968 documentó las inconsistencias y catalogó Levelland como uno de los casos rigorosos no explicados.
whatHappened_en:
Between 22:50 on November 2 and 01:30 on November 3, 1957, Sheriff Weir Clem of Hockley County, Texas received 15 independent calls from motorists within a 16 km radius around Levelland. All reported the same phenomenon: a bright oval object on or near the road; their engines died and headlights went out as they approached; as the object moved away the systems spontaneously restored.

Sheriff Clem and his deputy drove to the scene and themselves observed a bright red-orange object before it rose and disappeared. Pedro Saucedo, the first witness of the event, had stopped his vehicle fearing a collision; his engine and lights failed as the object passed over the vehicle and recovered after it left.

Project Blue Book investigated and attributed the event to 'ball lightning' — an insufficient explanation for 15 independent motorists with repeatable electrical effects on different vehicles over three hours in atmospherically normal weather (no thunderstorm reported). Dr. James McDonald's (University of Arizona) 1968 investigation documented the inconsistencies and cataloged Levelland as one of the rigorous unexplained cases.
whyMatters: Primer evento masivo documentado de interferencia electromagnética sobre vehículos civiles independientes, con confirmación por autoridad civil (sheriff) en tiempo real. El patrón de efectos EM recuperables al alejarse del objeto — observado luego en Coyne 1973, Tehran 1976 y decenas de casos posteriores — debuta en Levelland como dato estructurado. La explicación oficial 'ball lightning' es estadísticamente insuficiente y suele citarse como ejemplo paradigmático de desacreditación inadecuada en Blue Book.
whyMatters_en: The first documented mass event of electromagnetic interference on independent civilian vehicles, with real-time confirmation by a civil authority (the sheriff). The pattern of recoverable EM effects as the object moves away — later seen in Coyne 1973, Tehran 1976, and dozens of subsequent cases — debuts at Levelland as structured data. The official 'ball lightning' explanation is statistically insufficient and is often cited as a paradigmatic example of inadequate debunking in Blue Book.
